disclaimer: Educational policy tracking only. This is not legal advice, medical advice, treatment access guidance, or a substitute for checking current law with qualified counsel.

rows.action: 21 CFR 1308.11 federal Schedule I listing for Ibogaine
rows.primarySource: Cornell Legal Information Institute / eCFR mirror
rows.whatItPermits: Establishes the federal baseline that Ibogaine is listed in Schedule I under U.S. controlled-substances regulations.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Does not authorize medical treatment, prescribing, clinic access, or state-level exceptions that override federal law.
rows.federalCaveat: This remains the starting point for every U.S. state policy row unless and until federal law changes.

rows.action: FDA noribogaine IND-related clinical research action
rows.whatItPermits: DemeRx NB may begin a phase I noribogaine hydrochloride study in a closely monitored U.S. clinical setting.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Not FDA approval, not proof of safety or effectiveness, and not a general treatment access pathway.
rows.federalCaveat: Noribogaine research language is separate from Ibogaine treatment access.

rows.action: HB 2871, appropriation for Ibogaine clinical research study
rows.whatItPermits: The proposal would have appropriated state funds for a certified clinical research study on Ibogaine for neurological diseases.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: This tracker does not treat the proposal as current access or an enacted 2026 program without a newer official status source.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal Schedule I and FDA/DEA/IRB requirements would remain controlling.

rows.action: HB26-1325, Natural Medicine / Ibogaine research pilot program
rows.whatItPermits: Creates an Ibogaine research pilot program lane, allows up to five pilot sites, includes possible rulemaking around administration/manufacturing/use, and adds benefit-sharing language tied to Indigenous communities.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Does not make unsupervised Ibogaine use lawful and should not be read as FDA approval, proof of efficacy, or a provider referral pathway.
rows.federalCaveat: Any research or clinical activity remains constrained by federal law and applicable approvals.

rows.action: SB 77, Ibogaine research in the Commonwealth
rows.whatItPermits: Establishes a state framework for Ibogaine research and intellectual-property development through a public-private partnership approach.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: The enacted framework does not create general treatment access or FDA approval.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal Schedule I status and FDA approval requirements remain central.

rows.action: SB 43, psychedelic-assisted therapy / clinical research language
rows.whatItPermits: The bill record describes psychedelic-assisted therapy legislation and has included Ibogaine-related clinical-study discussion in public tracking.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Do not treat this as final law or treatment access until final enrollment/signature status is confirmed.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal law, FDA authorization, and state implementation details remain controlling.

rows.action: SB 527 / HB 1477, Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program
rows.whatItPermits: Would establish an Ibogaine Clinical Research Grant Program and include it as an authorized use of Opioid Restitution Fund money.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Introduced/hearing activity is not enactment and does not authorize treatment access.
rows.federalCaveat: Any funded research would still need applicable federal authorization.

rows.action: HB 314, Ibogaine Drug Development Clinical Trial Act
rows.primarySource: Mississippi Legislature bill text as sent to governor
rows.whatItPermits: Creates a state framework for an Ibogaine drug-development clinical trial consortium and coordination with a lead consortium in another state.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Does not provide routine clinical access; treatment-administration provisions depend on FDA approval or lawful federal authorization.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal waiver, authorization, IND, and FDA approval language remains central.

rows.primarySource: Ohio Legislative Service Commission board record
rows.whatItPermits: Creates and maintains a temporary study committee to evaluate Ibogaine treatment issues and make legislative recommendations.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: A study committee is not legalization, treatment access, a clinical trial authorization, or FDA approval.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal Schedule I status remains unchanged.

rows.whatItPermits: Creates a state framework related to Ibogaine clinical trials and drug-development requirements.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Does not make Ibogaine FDA-approved and does not by itself authorize unsupervised treatment or provider referral.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal Schedule I status and FDA/DEA/IRB requirements remain central.

rows.action: HB 4293, Veterans Mental Health Innovation Act
rows.whatItPermits: Would authorize scientific research and clinical trials related to Ibogaine with registration and immunity language.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Introduced/referred language is not enactment and does not create general treatment access.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal authorization and controlled-substance constraints remain central.

rows.whatItPermits: Would allow an attending physician to provide Ibogaine to a patient for specified disorders and exempt specified use from controlled-substance definition if enacted.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: As an in-committee bill, it does not create current legal access or override federal law.
rows.federalCaveat: DEA/FDA constraints and federal Schedule I status remain unresolved.

rows.whatItPermits: Authorizes Tennessee research institutions to participate in federally authorized clinical trials involving Ibogaine under specified safety and compliance conditions.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Does not authorize routine clinical treatment, non-research possession, or self-directed access.
rows.federalCaveat: Clinical work must comply with a valid FDA IND or other federal authorization when required.

rows.action: SB 2308, Ibogaine drug development clinical trials
rows.whatItPermits: Creates a pathway for a selected consortium and interagency contract for Ibogaine drug development clinical trials.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Treatment-administration provisions apply only if FDA approves Ibogaine to treat a medical condition.
rows.federalCaveat: Implementation may require federal waiver or authorization; clinical work remains subject to federal law.

rows.action: State-funded IMPACT Ibogaine clinical trials program
rows.primarySource: Texas Tribune reporting with state-program context
rows.whatItPermits: Tracks Texas' move toward state-run or state-funded clinical trials after difficulty finding a drug-company partner.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Reporting about implementation does not mean treatment access, FDA approval, or proof that trials are already enrolling.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal law and trial authorization remain central.

rows.action: H.859, psychedelic therapy and Ibogaine clinical drug development trials
rows.whatItPermits: Would establish a Psychedelic Therapy Advisory Board and require the Department of Health to contract with a Vermont entity for Ibogaine clinical drug-development trials.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Introduced bill language is not enactment and does not authorize treatment access.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal authorization remains required for clinical drug-development work.

rows.action: HB 4626, grant program for FDA drug-development trials with Ibogaine
rows.whatItPermits: Would have established a grant program to fund FDA drug-development trials with Ibogaine.
rows.whatItDoesNotPermit: Because it was vetoed, it should not be treated as current law or active access.
rows.federalCaveat: Federal Schedule I and FDA approval constraints remain unchanged.
